newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST SLALOM RUN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST SLALOM RUN.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg led after the first leg of a women's Alpine skiing World Cup slalom on Saturday.
Wiberg mastered the icy hard Hirschenkogel piste, flagged with 58 gates, in 51.18 seconds on a bitterly cold day.
Wiberg, an Olympic and world champion, was followed by Austria's 1993 overall World Cup winner Anita Wachter (51.61).
Austrian-born Claudia Riegler, who races for her mother's country's New Zealand after a disagreement with her native ski federation, was third in 51.69.
Riegler, aiming for her third consecutive slalom victory this season, promised to "give it all" in the second run which was due to start at 1000 GMT.
She won the only other slaloms staged so far this season at Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana, Switzerland.
Switzerland's Sonja Nef was fourth in the first leg in 51.85, followed by Sweden's Ylva Nowen (51.90) and Italy's Deborah Compagnoni (51.92).
